title: Mitigate streaming backpressure disconnects causing partial responses
creator: Asha Patel
description: Postmortem follow-up for the 2026-02-23 streaming outages where client connections frequently experienced disconnects and partial token delivery under high QPS. Symptom: streaming responses truncated mid-token or connection closed after a variable number of tokens (5-200). Scope: affected hosted API endpoints for several customers during a capacity spike; Dedicated pools that had a recent runtime kernel selection change also saw elevated error rates. Immediate remediation (hotfix rollback) restored stability but root causes and durable fixes are required.
incident_summary: On 2026-02-23 (~15:42 UTC) we observed elevated 5xx and broken-stream errors on /v1/stream endpoints. Error rates peaked for ~18 minutes correlated with a sustained influx of short requests that caused unlucky packing and long tail kernel stalls; requests hit connection-level buffering limits and the proxy closed streams when upstream write buffers filled. A code change in kernel selection (ENG-7370) changed scheduling heuristics and reduced fairness for small-latency requests which amplified backpressure. Autoscaler did not react fast enough due to conservative scaling thresholds.
root_causes: Regression in kernel selection heuristics (ENG-7370) reduced fairness for short requests leading to scheduler stalls under mixed workloads
No per-connection flow-control on the streaming proxy: upstream write buffer exhaustion produced abrupt disconnects instead of backpressure signals
KV-cache memory growth under certain quantization modes led to occasional GC-like pauses on the model workers
Autoscaler scaling window and thresholds were too conservative for sudden bursty QPS patterns observed in hosted tier
Insufficient synthetic load tests for streaming under mixed short-and-long request patterns (e2e coverage gap)
mitigation_taken: Rolled back ENG-7370 kernel selection heuristic change at 15:58 UTC which immediately lowered error rates
Temporarily raised streaming connection write buffer limit and increased connection timeout to 60s
Enabled an emergency autoscale policy for affected pools to increase headroom during the incident
Notified on-call SREs and paged product owners; created ticket ENG-7422 to inform customers and provide credits
action_items: Implement per-connection streaming flow-control (proxy-level); require explicit ACK or windowing from server to client (owner: Diego Morales, estimate: 5)
Add connection-level circuit breaker to gracefully reject new streams when downstream write buffers exceed safe thresholds (owner: SRE, estimate: 3)
Revert and add unit+integration tests around kernel selection fairness with mixed short/long request distributions (owner: runtime-team, estimate: 4)
Increase autoscaler responsiveness for hosted pools: add burst policy + reduce stabilization window; add synthetic burst tests (owner: infra, estimate: 3)
Investigation into KV cache growth and memory accounting under quantized model paths; patch memory leak if found (owner: model-runtime, estimate: 5)
Create a streaming outage runbook with clear escalation and customer communication templates (owner: SRE, estimate: 2)
Add regression smoke tests in CI that validate stream continuity and token completeness for 1k simulated concurrent streams (owner: qa, estimate: 6)
Post-incident customer outreach: targeted emails + dashboard status item for affected tenants (owner: Support, estimate: 2)
Add telemetry: per-connection buffer metrics, per-stream token counts, and end-to-end latency percentiles segmented by request length (owner: observability, estimate: 3)
acceptance_criteria: Streaming proxy exposes per-connection 'available window' metric and enforces flow-control without dropping in-flight tokens
No streaming disconnect spikes in staged synthetic burst tests for 48h with mixed request lengths
Kernel selection change reverted or reworked; unit/integration tests added and passing in CI
Autoscaler responds to 3x baseline QPS bursts within target SLO window in canary environment
Runbook published and on-call rotation updated; postmortem communicated to customers
reproduction_steps: Deploy runtime-1.24 with the kernel selection change enabled in a canary region
Run synthetic load: 2k concurrent clients with 70% short (<=64 tokens) and 30% long (>512 tokens) requests using streaming endpoint
Record per-connection buffer fill, write latency, and stream completion rate; observe disconnects/partial token deliveries
Toggle autoscaler thresholds to match production settings and observe scaling behavior under burst
Enable heap/memory profiling on a model worker to reproduce KV-cache growth pattern
